scenario.name: CrowdStrike, Kaspersky & Mandiant — Lazarus (SmoothOperator): 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain & Gopuram
scenario.shortSubtitle: Supply Chain · Signed 3CX Build Tamper, 0xFEEDFACE RC4 & GitHub .ico Dead-Drop
scenario.overview: Picture a gleaming white telecommunications assembly cleanroom where sleek business desk phones glide down an aluminum conveyor toward a heavy brass authenticity press. Just before an open phone reaches the press, a dark covert robotic arm drops from an upstream supplier vent and swaps in two rigged interior pieces: a crimson-toothed brass audio gear and a frosted glass prism hiding a glowing amber wax-sealed core inside its base. Moments later, the lid snaps shut and the official factory press stamps a completely genuine gold-and-emerald hologram right onto the phone top, so the quality inspector scans the authentic seal and waves it straight onto a trader office desk. Once plugged in at the desk, the phone shell splits open in cutaway: the rigged brass gear spins first, cracks open the amber core inside the frosted prism, and unwinds a glowing ribbon into a hidden micro-radio. That radio scans an innocent framed portrait tile hanging on a public art-gallery wall, peels a secret crimson address strip off the bottom border of the frame, siphons keycards right out of the trader desk folder, and opens a private beam to an elevated high-value vault while a violet behavioral watch monitor catches a desk telephone reaching into a credential drawer. In this scenario (CVE-2023-29059, MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002, T1574.002, T1102.001, and T1555.003) documented jointly by CrowdStrike, Mandiant, and Kaspersky, Lazarus Group compromises the 3CX Windows build server via an upstream X_TRADER breach and ships a validly signed trojanized VoIP installer to WKS-TRD-14. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: pre-signing tampering of ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll, then DLL side-loading and 0xFEEDFACE RC4 decryption into unbacked RWX RAM, then GitHub IconStorages .ico steganographic C2 resolution, then ICONICSTEALER credential theft paired with selective Stage-2 Gopuram backdoor deployment. Steps #1-#4 trace the full kill chain, while Memory Forensics compares clean vs. trojanized d3dcompiler_47.dll alongside unbacked RWX implant regions.

memoryBlocks.description: Trojanized graphics compiler library shipped inside the validly signed 3CX installer. Clean Microsoft Direct3D sections sit intact at the front while an appended 312 KB RC4-encrypted SmoothOperator payload hides directly after the 4-byte magic marker FE ED FA CE (0xFEEDFACE).

Unbacked MEM_PRIVATE PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE memory region allocated via VirtualAlloc by side-loaded ffmpeg.dll. Holds the freshly RC4-decrypted shellcode loader that waits through its delay window, downloads GitHub IconStorages .ico files, and slices the hidden Base64 C2 trailer past image EOF.

Stage-2 in-memory payload fetched after resolving akamaitechcloudservices[.]com from icon12.ico. ICONICSTEALER harvests Chrome and Edge credential stores while high-value finance and crypto victims selectively receive the modular Gopuram espionage backdoor inside PID 7120.

stages.title: Cascading Build Compromise & Signed Trojanized Installer (X_TRADER -> 3CX)
stages.subtitle: Trojanized ffmpeg.dll & d3dcompiler_47.dll Sealed Under Valid 3CX Authenticode
stages.description: Inside the sterile telecommunications assembly cleanroom, an open matte-white business phone glides down the belt. Seconds before it enters the official sealing station, a dark robotic arm drops from an upstream supplier vent, places a crimson-toothed brass audio gear and a frosted prism housing a hidden amber core inside the chassis, and retracts, allowing the official gold press to emboss a 100% genuine emerald-gold authenticity hologram onto the closed lid so the warehouse inspector waves it straight to the customer desk. Mandiant UNC4736 investigation uncovered that the 3CX breach was a historic cascading supply-chain attack: Lazarus Group first compromised an older financial trading application called X_TRADER, used that foothold to infect a 3CX engineer workstation, and pivoted directly into the 3CX Windows build server. Inside that CI/CD build environment, the attackers replaced two bundled Electron dependencies, ffmpeg.dll (the audio/video helper library) and d3dcompiler_47.dll (a Direct3D shader compiler library padded with an encrypted payload), BEFORE the automated signing pipeline applied the genuine 3CX Ltd. Extended Validation Authenticode certificate. When trading workstation WKS-TRD-14 (10.10.8.41) installs 3CXDesktopApp v18.12.407, Windows signature validation passes 100% green because the outer MSI and 3CXDesktopApp.exe binary truly were signed by 3CX. Code signing proves publisher integrity only from the moment the signing step runs onward (never guaranteeing the cleanliness of upstream build inputs). Because Lazarus altered ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll inside the build workspace prior to packaging (leaving ffmpeg.dll unsigned and inflating d3dcompiler_47.dll to 4.4 MB with a high-entropy trailing overlay), Sysmon Event ID 11 (FileCreate capturing installation under AppData\Local\Programs\3CXDesktopApp\app-18.12.407\) and Sysmon Event ID 7 (ImageLoaded flagging Signed = false on ffmpeg.dll loaded by a validly signed parent executable) expose the discrepancy between the trusted outer signature and its tampered companion DLLs. On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SIGNED TROJAN INSTALL / ⇠#1 ACK Signed Valid) from Node ① (#1 3CX Build Server (X_TRADER Pivot)) to Node ② (#2 Enterprise TLS Proxy), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike Falcon EDR & Sysmon).

stages.title: DLL Side-Loading (ffmpeg.dll) & 0xFEEDFACE RC4 Shellcode Decryption
stages.subtitle: VirtualAlloc RWX Decryption Inside Legitimately Signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe
stages.description: Plugged in on the trader office desk, the sealed business phone powers up and splits open cleanly in cutaway. The rigged crimson-toothed brass audio gear spins first, extends an extractor fork to crack the bottom seam of the frosted glass prism, pulls out the glowing amber wax-sealed core, and unwinds its spinning golden cipher ribbon into a hovering holographic micro-radio right inside the phone cavity. The instant user CORP\d.chen launches 3CXDesktopApp.exe (PID 7120), Windows DLL search order loads the co-located trojanized ffmpeg.dll (situated in the exact same application folder as the executable). Inside its hijacked export routine (such as av_buffer_create), ffmpeg.dll opens its neighbor file d3dcompiler_47.dll, scans forward until it spots the exact 4-byte magic marker 0xFEEDFACE (FE ED FA CE, acting as a bookmark separating clean Direct3D code from the hidden payload), reads the trailing 312 KB encrypted blob, calls VirtualAlloc to reserve an unbacked MEM_PRIVATE PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE region at 0x000001C948200000 (anonymous RAM not tied to any signed file on disk with simultaneous read, write, and execute permissions so decrypted shellcode can run immediately), and decrypts the SmoothOperator shellcode in memory using the RC4 stream cipher with key "3jB(2bsG#@c7". Splitting the loader across two companion DLLs (tiny trigger logic inside ffmpeg.dll plus an encrypted blob appended past the clean PE sections of Microsoft d3dcompiler_47.dll after 0xFEEDFACE) ensures static antivirus scanners inspecting either file alone see mostly legitimate open-source FFmpeg or Direct3D code. At runtime, however, executing decrypted instructions inside an unbacked MEM_PRIVATE RWX allocation (0x000001C948200000) inside an Electron VoIP phone triggers high-confidence EDR memory scans and YARA rules matching FE ED FA CE combined with the RC4 key string. On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ 0xFEEDFACE RC4 / ⇠#2 ALERT 0xFEEDFACE) from Node ② (#2 Enterprise TLS Proxy) to Node ③ (#3 Trading Desk Workstation (WKS-TRD-14)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike Falcon EDR & Sysmon).

stages.title: GitHub IconStorages .ico Dead-Drop Resolver & C2 Resolution
stages.subtitle: Appended Base64 C2 String Hidden Past Valid .ico Image EOF
stages.description: Now humming inside the desk phone, the hidden holographic radio casts a thin cyan scan beam across a public art-gallery wall lined with six innocent framed portrait tiles. As the beam lands on tile number four, a concealed crimson paper ribbon peels cleanly off the bottom frame border, revealing secret coordinates tucked behind an ordinary public picture while ordinary observers see only a normal gallery wall. To prevent network defenders from immediately blocking a hardcoded malicious IP address, and to outwait automated sandboxes, the SmoothOperator shellcode sleeps for several days before fetching its live Command-and-Control address from a public GitHub dead-drop repository (raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon1.ico through icon16.ico). Each downloaded .ico file renders as a completely normal Windows icon image if opened, but Lazarus appended an encrypted Base64 string strictly past the image End-of-File marker. The in-memory loader slices off that trailing Base64 strip, decrypts it to obtain the live lookalike domain (akamaitechcloudservices[.]com), and initiates HTTPS staging. Abusing raw.githubusercontent.com as a Dead-Drop Resolver (MITRE T1102.001) lets the attacker blend C2 discovery into encrypted TLS 1.3 traffic destined for a universally trusted developer CDN while allowing instant C2 rotation simply by uploading updated .ico tiles. Even so, correlating Sysmon Event ID 22 (DNSQuery) and Sysmon Event ID 3 (NetworkConnect) immediately reveals a glaring process-to-network anomaly: a corporate desk VoIP phone (3CXDesktopApp.exe) has zero legitimate operational reason to download .ico files from a random GitHub repository and pivot to newly registered lookalike domains. In the documented Sysmon EID 22 + EID 3 exchange from Trading Desk Workstation (WKS-TRD-14) to 3CXDesktopApp.exe → ffmpeg.dll (RWX), 3CXDesktopApp.exe → ffmpeg.dll (RWX) responds with RESP icon12.ico (confirming that the GITHUB .ICO DEAD-DROP request succeeded on 3CXDesktopApp.exe → ffmpeg.dll (RWX) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #4 ICONICSTEALER Browser Vault Theft & Selective Gopuram Backdoor). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GITHUB .ICO DEAD-DROP / ⇠#3 RESP icon12.ico) from Node ③ (#3 Trading Desk Workstation (WKS-TRD-14)) to Node ④ (#4 3CXDesktopApp.exe → ffmpeg.dll (RWX)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike Falcon EDR & Sysmon).

stages.title: ICONICSTEALER Browser Vault Theft & Selective Gopuram Backdoor
stages.subtitle: VoIP App Reading Chrome Login Data & Targeted Finance Espionage
stages.description: Guided by the peeled gallery address strip, the desk phone opens a quiet siphon straight into the trader desktop browser folder, lifting glowing blue keycards out of the vault while an elevated crimson private vault locks onto this high-value trading desk, at the exact instant the violet behavioral watch monitor flashes an unmistakable alarm because a desk telephone has no business reaching into a password drawer. After connecting to akamaitechcloudservices[.]com, 3CXDesktopApp.exe loads the Stage-2 ICONICSTEALER module in RAM (0x000001C948280000) to collect system identity, domain membership, and saved browser credential databases from Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Firefox (specifically targeting User Data\Default\Login Data and Local State). Kaspersky GReAT discovered that Lazarus operated with surgical selectivity: for thousands of ordinary 3CX victims, the intrusion paused at reconnaissance, whereas select high-value cryptocurrency exchanges and financial institutions like WKS-TRD-14 received the sophisticated second-stage Gopuram modular backdoor for long-term espionage. This final stage illustrates why CrowdStrike Falcon OverWatch caught the global campaign before anyone knew the 3CX installer itself was compromised: even though 3CXDesktopApp.exe carried a 100% valid Authenticode signature, behavioral EDR telemetry flagged a desktop telephone executable opening Chrome and Edge Login Data files and establishing anomalous TLS C2 sessions (loading Gopuram at 0x000001C948280000). Enforcing behavioral process-boundary rules on browser credential stores stops signed supply-chain implants on Day Zero. On the diagram, follow Step #4 / Link #4 (#4→ STEALER + GOPURAM / ⇠#4 ALERT Gopuram C2) from Node ④ (#4 3CXDesktopApp.exe → ffmpeg.dll (RWX)) to Node ⑤ (#5 Chrome Login Data & Lazarus C2), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CrowdStrike Falcon EDR & Sysmon).

detectionRule.title: Signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe Loading Trojanized ffmpeg.dll & Oversized d3dcompiler_47.dll
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: 3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain Trojanized DLL Side-Load
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: image_load
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\3CXDesktopApp.exe'
    ImageLoaded|endswith:
      - '\ffmpeg.dll'
      - '\d3dcompiler_47.dll'
    Signed: 'false'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) hash verification on CI/CD release artifacts and alert when a legitimately signed Electron executable loads unsigned or size-anomalous DLLs.

detectionRule.title: 3CX d3dcompiler_47.dll 0xFEEDFACE Encrypted Shellcode Marker
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule Lazarus_3CX_FEEDFACE_RC4_Loader {
  meta:
    author = "CrowdStrike & Mandiant DFIR"
    cve = "CVE-2023-29059"
    severity = "critical"
  strings:
    $magic = { FE ED FA CE }
    $rc4_key = "3jB(2bsG#@c7" ascii
    $github = "IconStorages/images/main/icon" ascii
  condition:
    $magic and ($rc4_key or $github)
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Monitor signed desktop applications for VirtualAlloc PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE allocations originating from side-loaded DLLs and scan companion DLL overlays for high-entropy trailers.

detectionRule.title: Non-Browser Signed Desktop Application Accessing Chromium Login Data Vault
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: VoIP or Non-Browser App Reading Browser Credential Databases
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: file_access
detection:
  selection_target:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data'
      - '\Edge\User Data\Default\Login Data'
  filter_browsers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
  condition: selection_target and not filter_browsers
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Deploy behavioral EDR rules blocking non-browser processes from reading Chromium Login Data and Local State files regardless of valid code signatures.

The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: pre-signing tampering of ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll, then DLL side-loading and 0xFEEDFACE RC4 decryption into unbacked RWX RAM, then GitHub IconStorages .ico steganographic C2 resolution, then ICONICSTEALER credential theft paired with selective Stage-2 Gopuram backdoor deployment. Steps #1-#4 trace the full kill chain, while Memory Forensics compares clean vs. trojanized d3dcompiler_47.dll alongside unbacked RWX implant regions.
briefing.diagramTopologySummary: On the diagram: Follow Step #1 from Node ① (3CX Build Pipeline) shipping the signed trojanized installer to Node ② (WKS-TRD-14), watch Step #2 execute inside Node ③ (3CXDesktopApp.exe PID 7120) decrypting Node ④ (0xFEEDFACE & RWX RAM), trace Step #3 fetching Node ⑤ (GitHub IconStorages .ico Dead-Drop), and see Step #4 trigger Node ⑥ (CrowdStrike / EDR Watch) as the VoIP app reads browser vaults.

steps.plainTitle: Pre-Signing Cleanroom Tamper & Genuine Authenticode Seal Delivery
steps.storyAnalogy: Inside the sterile telecommunications assembly cleanroom, an open matte-white business phone glides down the belt. Seconds before it enters the official sealing station, a dark robotic arm drops from an upstream supplier vent, places a crimson-toothed brass audio gear and a frosted prism housing a hidden amber core inside the chassis, and retracts, allowing the official gold press to emboss a 100% genuine emerald-gold authenticity hologram onto the closed lid so the warehouse inspector waves it straight to the customer desk.
steps.simpleExplanation: Mandiant UNC4736 investigation uncovered that the 3CX breach was a historic cascading supply-chain attack: Lazarus Group first compromised an older financial trading application called X_TRADER, used that foothold to infect a 3CX engineer workstation, and pivoted directly into the 3CX Windows build server. Inside that CI/CD build environment, the attackers replaced two bundled Electron dependencies, ffmpeg.dll (the audio/video helper library) and d3dcompiler_47.dll (a Direct3D shader compiler library padded with an encrypted payload), BEFORE the automated signing pipeline applied the genuine 3CX Ltd. Extended Validation Authenticode certificate. When trading workstation WKS-TRD-14 (10.10.8.41) installs 3CXDesktopApp v18.12.407, Windows signature validation passes 100% green because the outer MSI and 3CXDesktopApp.exe binary truly were signed by 3CX.
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Code signing proves publisher integrity only from the moment the signing step runs onward (never guaranteeing the cleanliness of upstream build inputs). Because Lazarus altered ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll inside the build workspace prior to packaging (leaving ffmpeg.dll unsigned and inflating d3dcompiler_47.dll to 4.4 MB with a high-entropy trailing overlay), Sysmon Event ID 11 (FileCreate capturing installation under AppData\Local\Programs\3CXDesktopApp\app-18.12.407\) and Sysmon Event ID 7 (ImageLoaded flagging Signed = false on ffmpeg.dll loaded by a validly signed parent executable) expose the discrepancy between the trusted outer signature and its tampered companion DLLs.
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, Step #1 ships from Node ① (3CX Build Pipeline) to Node ② (WKS-TRD-14 10.10.8.41), installing Node ③ (3CXDesktopApp.exe PID 7120) while Node ⑥ (CrowdStrike / EDR Watch) logs the unsigned ffmpeg.dll image load.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event ID 7 (validly signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe loading unsigned trojanized ffmpeg.dll and oversized d3dcompiler_47.dll) correlated with Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) hash verification against clean Microsoft d3dcompiler_47.dll.

steps.plainTitle: Side-Loading ffmpeg.dll & RC4-Decrypting the 0xFEEDFACE Payload Into RWX RAM
steps.storyAnalogy: Plugged in on the trader office desk, the sealed business phone powers up and splits open cleanly in cutaway. The rigged crimson-toothed brass audio gear spins first, extends an extractor fork to crack the bottom seam of the frosted glass prism, pulls out the glowing amber wax-sealed core, and unwinds its spinning golden cipher ribbon into a hovering holographic micro-radio right inside the phone cavity.
steps.simpleExplanation: The instant user CORP\d.chen launches 3CXDesktopApp.exe (PID 7120), Windows DLL search order loads the co-located trojanized ffmpeg.dll (situated in the exact same application folder as the executable). Inside its hijacked export routine (such as av_buffer_create), ffmpeg.dll opens its neighbor file d3dcompiler_47.dll, scans forward until it spots the exact 4-byte magic marker 0xFEEDFACE (FE ED FA CE, acting as a bookmark separating clean Direct3D code from the hidden payload), reads the trailing 312 KB encrypted blob, calls VirtualAlloc to reserve an unbacked MEM_PRIVATE PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE region at 0x000001C948200000 (anonymous RAM not tied to any signed file on disk with simultaneous read, write, and execute permissions so decrypted shellcode can run immediately), and decrypts the SmoothOperator shellcode in memory using the RC4 stream cipher with key "3jB(2bsG#@c7".
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Splitting the loader across two companion DLLs (tiny trigger logic inside ffmpeg.dll plus an encrypted blob appended past the clean PE sections of Microsoft d3dcompiler_47.dll after 0xFEEDFACE) ensures static antivirus scanners inspecting either file alone see mostly legitimate open-source FFmpeg or Direct3D code. At runtime, however, executing decrypted instructions inside an unbacked MEM_PRIVATE RWX allocation (0x000001C948200000) inside an Electron VoIP phone triggers high-confidence EDR memory scans and YARA rules matching FE ED FA CE combined with the RC4 key string.
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, Step #2 executes inside Node ③ (3CXDesktopApp.exe PID 7120), carving Node ④ (0xFEEDFACE & RWX RAM at 0x000001C948200000) while Node ⑥ (CrowdStrike / EDR Watch) raises a memory-integrity YARA match.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in EDR Memory / YARA Scans (FE ED FA CE overlay marker inside d3dcompiler_47.dll and RC4 key 3jB(2bsG#@c7) paired with unbacked MEM_PRIVATE RWX allocations at 0x000001C948200000 inside signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe.

steps.plainTitle: Peeling Hidden C2 Addresses Off Innocent GitHub IconStorages .ico Tiles
steps.storyAnalogy: Now humming inside the desk phone, the hidden holographic radio casts a thin cyan scan beam across a public art-gallery wall lined with six innocent framed portrait tiles. As the beam lands on tile number four, a concealed crimson paper ribbon peels cleanly off the bottom frame border, revealing secret coordinates tucked behind an ordinary public picture while ordinary observers see only a normal gallery wall.
steps.simpleExplanation: To prevent network defenders from immediately blocking a hardcoded malicious IP address, and to outwait automated sandboxes, the SmoothOperator shellcode sleeps for several days before fetching its live Command-and-Control address from a public GitHub dead-drop repository (raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon1.ico through icon16.ico). Each downloaded .ico file renders as a completely normal Windows icon image if opened, but Lazarus appended an encrypted Base64 string strictly past the image End-of-File marker. The in-memory loader slices off that trailing Base64 strip, decrypts it to obtain the live lookalike domain (akamaitechcloudservices[.]com), and initiates HTTPS staging.
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Abusing raw.githubusercontent.com as a Dead-Drop Resolver (MITRE T1102.001) lets the attacker blend C2 discovery into encrypted TLS 1.3 traffic destined for a universally trusted developer CDN while allowing instant C2 rotation simply by uploading updated .ico tiles. Even so, correlating Sysmon Event ID 22 (DNSQuery) and Sysmon Event ID 3 (NetworkConnect) immediately reveals a glaring process-to-network anomaly: a corporate desk VoIP phone (3CXDesktopApp.exe) has zero legitimate operational reason to download .ico files from a random GitHub repository and pivot to newly registered lookalike domains.
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, Step #3 shoots from Node ③ (3CXDesktopApp.exe PID 7120) to Node ⑤ (GitHub IconStorages & C2 via icon12.ico) while Node ⑥ (CrowdStrike / EDR Watch) logs Sysmon Event ID 22 and Event ID 3.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event ID 22 & Event ID 3 (3CXDesktopApp.exe resolving raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon12.ico and pivoting to akamaitechcloudservices[.]com) and Suricata TLS/SNI dead-drop alerts.

steps.plainTitle: ICONICSTEALER Browser Vault Theft & Selective Stage-2 Gopuram Backdoor
steps.storyAnalogy: Guided by the peeled gallery address strip, the desk phone opens a quiet siphon straight into the trader desktop browser folder, lifting glowing blue keycards out of the vault while an elevated crimson private vault locks onto this high-value trading desk, at the exact instant the violet behavioral watch monitor flashes an unmistakable alarm because a desk telephone has no business reaching into a password drawer.
steps.simpleExplanation: After connecting to akamaitechcloudservices[.]com, 3CXDesktopApp.exe loads the Stage-2 ICONICSTEALER module in RAM (0x000001C948280000) to collect system identity, domain membership, and saved browser credential databases from Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Firefox (specifically targeting User Data\Default\Login Data and Local State). Kaspersky GReAT discovered that Lazarus operated with surgical selectivity: for thousands of ordinary 3CX victims, the intrusion paused at reconnaissance, whereas select high-value cryptocurrency exchanges and financial institutions like WKS-TRD-14 received the sophisticated second-stage Gopuram modular backdoor for long-term espionage.
steps.howItWorksInPractice: This final stage illustrates why CrowdStrike Falcon OverWatch caught the global campaign before anyone knew the 3CX installer itself was compromised: even though 3CXDesktopApp.exe carried a 100% valid Authenticode signature, behavioral EDR telemetry flagged a desktop telephone executable opening Chrome and Edge Login Data files and establishing anomalous TLS C2 sessions (loading Gopuram at 0x000001C948280000). Enforcing behavioral process-boundary rules on browser credential stores stops signed supply-chain implants on Day Zero.
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, Step #4 pulls browser credentials from Node ② (WKS-TRD-14) through Node ③ (3CXDesktopApp.exe) toward Node ⑤ (Gopuram C2) while Node ⑥ (CrowdStrike / EDR Watch) fires the definitive behavioral alert.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in CrowdStrike / Kaspersky Behavioral EDR Alerts (signed 3CXDesktopApp.exe reading Chrome/Edge Login Data via ICONICSTEALER) correlated with selective Stage-2 Gopuram TLS C2 traffic.
